key_insight: AIPatient Arena shows that medical LLMs can sound strong in interviews and explanations, but still struggle with uncertainty, coverage, and diagnostic reasoning across realistic multi-turn consultations.
clinical_relevance: For AI-in-clinic screening, workflow-based evaluation matters more than final-answer accuracy because it better reflects how models gather, interpret, and communicate patient information.
method: Built an EHR-grounded evaluation framework using patient-specific knowledge graphs
Simulated multi-turn physician-patient consultations across eight clinical competence dimensions
Tested on 437 primary patients plus 119 and 67 out-of-distribution validation patients
evidence_signal: Across cohorts, LLMs scored highest on questioning, professionalism, and explanation clarity, but weaker on ambiguity handling, information coverage, and diagnostic accuracy.
watch_item: High performance in scripted evaluation does not guarantee safe real-world use, especially when models repeat questions, omit history, or handle uncertainty poorly.
paper_title: AIPatient Arena: EHR-grounded evaluation of large language models in end-to-end clinical consultation workflows
